settings.heading: Design your piece
settings.text: Most of what we make has never existed before. A bespoke commission is not a premium service here — it is the ordinary way the house works. It costs no more than a stock design of the same specification.
settings.image_alt: A graphite ring design sketch on tracing paper beside a carved wax model and loose diamonds

settings.heading: A conversation, then a drawing, then a wax
settings.text: You arrive with something — a photograph, an heirloom, a shape you cannot name. We draw until it is right, source the stone to your brief, and cut the piece for the hand that will wear it. You approve every stage. Nothing is bought until you have seen it.

settings.title: Consultation
settings.text: An hour, in the atelier or by video. We talk about the wearer, how they use their hands, the occasion and the budget — before anything is drawn. Bring photographs of anything you love, including things that are not jewellery.

settings.title: Design
settings.text: Hand drawings first, because they are quicker to argue with. Then a scaled rendering showing profile, gallery and band width from every angle. Two rounds of revision are included; almost nobody needs a third.

settings.title: Stone selection
settings.text: We source to your brief through two Antwerp houses and show you three or four candidates loose, under the same light, with their certificates. You will be told plainly what you are paying for and what you are not.

settings.title: Craftsmanship
settings.text: Carved in wax, cast in your metal, then set, filed, emeried and polished by hand at the bench. Hallmarked at the London Assay Office with the year it was made. We photograph it before it leaves.

settings.title: Delivery
settings.text: Collected in the atelier with a glass of something, or delivered insured and signed-for anywhere in the world, in a box made for the piece. Your certificate and valuation travel with it.

settings.heading: Five steps, six to nine weeks
settings.text: The same sequence whether you are remodelling an heirloom or starting from a blank sheet.

settings.image_alt: A goldsmith setting a diamond into a gold ring with fine steel tools
settings.heading: The parts a photograph never shows
settings.text:
A ring is judged from above and worn from the side. The gallery under the stone, the taper of the shank, the height of the setting against a knuckle — these decide whether it is comfortable in ten years, and none of them appear in a product photograph.

That is what the wax stage is for. You hold the shape before it is metal.

settings.title: No bespoke premium
settings.text: A commission costs the same as a stock design of the same metal, stone and setting. You pay for materials and bench hours, not for the word.

settings.title: Nothing bought blind
settings.text: Drawings before stones, stones before casting, casting before payment in full. You can stop at any stage.

settings.title: Yours alone
settings.text: We do not repeat a bespoke design for another client. The drawings stay in your file.

settings.question: How long does a commission take?
settings.answer: Six to nine weeks from approved drawing to hallmark. A sourced stone or an unusually complex setting can add two to three weeks, and we will tell you before you commit rather than after.

settings.question: What does it cost?
settings.answer: The same as a stock design of the same specification. Most engagement commissions sit between £2,500 and £12,000; the stone is usually two thirds of that. We quote a fixed price after the design stage and it does not move.

settings.question: Do I need to know what I want?
settings.answer: No. Roughly half of our clients arrive with a photograph of something they do not actually like, which is still useful information. Bring anything — a building, a piece of furniture, a colour.

settings.question: Can you use my own stone or remodel an heirloom?
settings.answer: Often, yes. We will assess the stone for chips and check the setting is viable before we accept it, and we will be honest if remodelling would risk a piece that ought to be left alone.

settings.question: Natural or lab-grown?
settings.answer: Both, and we will never pretend one is the other. A lab-grown stone typically lets you go one to two carats further for the same budget. A natural stone holds resale value that a lab-grown one does not. Neither answer is wrong.

settings.question: Can I visit the atelier?
settings.answer: Yes, by appointment, on Clerkenwell Green. Consultations are also held by video, and about a third of our commissions are made for clients we never meet in person.

settings.question: What if I do not like the finished piece?
settings.answer: It has not happened, because you approve the drawing, the wax and the stone. Bespoke commissions are not returnable, and we say so plainly before you pay a deposit.
